name: The Muckross Abbey Yew

location.address: Muckross Friary (Muckross Abbey), Killarney National Park, Co. Kerry; centre of the cloister garth

official_register.name: Ancient Yew Group database, Muckross Friary tree 2017

access: Unguided Heritage Ireland (OPW) site inside Killarney National Park; no admission or opening hours seen on the Heritage Ireland page. Check the page for any change.
transport: About 4 km south-east of Killarney town centre; no public bus verified, jaunting car, bike or walk from town or Muckross House.
verify_notes: Heritage Ireland (fetched, OPW, owner of the site): 'a yew tree still stands at the centre [of the cloister]; thought to be one of the oldest in Ireland, as it is likely up to 400 years old'; Charles Smith in 1756 called it one of the tallest yews he had seen, 'its spreading branches, like a great umbrella, overshadow the niches of the great cloister'. Ancient Yew Group (fetched, tree 2017, Tim Hills, visit 20 Jul 2005): male, girth 305 cm at the ground; Ben Simon (Belfast City Council) 1999: 3.30 m at 0.6 m, 3.11 m at 1.5 m; Lowe 1897 recorded 10 ft at ground; earliest mention 1776, Arthur Young's Tour of Ireland; 'red-barked and twisted bole' rising from the centre of the cloister, branching at about 14 ft, elder rooted in its platform. CONFLICT on age: Heritage Ireland up to 400 years; tradition (Irish Examiner, thinplacestour, not fetched in full) says as old as the friary (founded 1448, about 575 years), and an Irish Examiner columnist suggests older; age is not measurable in a hollow yew, so the range is broad and no tradition is stated as fact. Friary founded about 1448 by Donal McCarthy Mor for the Observant Franciscans (Heritage Ireland). Pin: OSM way 1144959847 'Muckross Abbey' ambulatory, bbox centre 52.02614,-9.49479; the sources put the tree at the centre of the cloister, so within about 5-10 m. Second fine yew outside the ruin, close to the entrance, in a circular stone wall: Ancient Yew tree 2018, male, 399 cm at 60 cm, Lowe 1897 10 ft at ground (folded here as a note, not a separate collectible). Alive: Heritage Ireland present tense, lifecheck RECENT 2026-08-19 (iNaturalist at the abbey). Recognition line candidate: the huge red-barked yew rising out of the middle of the ruined cloister, its crown filling the open courtyard.
